what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 3 of 3: Why the measured kernel sits below the linear one when the theory says above. GIVEN (refereed): in backward 3+1 the one-step mean map of the transverse field is g phi(k) with g = 1 - 1/(n^2 beta^2) + ..., the O(1/beta) correction vanishes and the return sum drops out; a naive expansion predicted a ratio ABOVE 1. EXECUTED: measured S(k)(1 - |phi|^2)/sigma^2 at small k is 0.95-0.99 at beta = 2..6 and 1.01 at beta = 24 (backward), 1.01-1.09 (light-cone, beta = 1..2). The estimator (probes/lib/formation_levelplane.py) uses LAB-FRAME transverse components s.t1, s.t2 about the INITIAL direction, keeps the zero mode out of the shells, and sigma^2 = A(n beta)/(n beta). TASK: a formula that matches the table. Candidates: the lab-frame component is sin(theta) not theta (factor ~ 1 - <theta^2>); the mean direction wanders on a finite plane so 'transverse to the initial direction' mixes in longitudinal fluctuations; the noise of the record is not sigma^2 but the vMF transverse variance at the fluctuating concentration beta|S_x|; g < 1 shifts the pole.
